cost: THE SUBJECT LANDS ON THE TOP EDGE OF HIS BAND AND THAT EDGE IS A WALL, NOT A TUNING CHOICE. 84 against 80 +-4. The frontier is MARK JACKSON '98: pinned 55 +-3 by recal_109, reading 53, and he played 29.4 minutes against John Stockton '01's 29.2. Any factor monotone in minutes therefore pays the subject at least what it pays Jackson, and the two men's room is not compatible below 84 — Jackson can lose 16.6% of his term and the subject must lose 13.7% to reach 84 and 26.3% to reach 83. MEASURED rather than argued: 13,236 parameterisations of the whole floor-plus-ramp minutes family (floor 0.00 to 1.00 in steps of 0.02, foot 15.0 to 39.5 in half-minutes, width 0.5 to 25 minutes) hold every OFF anchor on the board - value and order, the only scale this round can move - and the LOWEST reading any of them gives the subject is 84. The only shape that separates two cards two tenths of a minute apart is a cliff at 29.3 mpg, which is a name check wearing a gate, and Mark Jackson '00 (27.0 mpg, pinned 58 +-3) closes it independently: a ramp that steep zeroes his whole term.

THE SIZE IS THE CLASS'S OWN UPPER QUARTILE AND IT IS MEASURED, NOT FITTED TO STOCKTON. Of the 834 cards the term pays, the 75th percentile of minutes is 34.7 (p10 22.8, median 31.6, p90 36.8) — the minutes at which a distributor in this class has carried a full season's creation. It also sits inside the window his own standing anchors leave: 33.9 to 35.2 all put the subject on 84 with every anchor held (33.8 leaves him on 85; 35.3 takes Mark Jackson '98 below his band), and 34.7 has 0.8 of a minute below it and 0.5 above.

recal_123's RECORDED CONSISTENCY DEFECT IS HALF-FIXED, ON PURPOSE. Its COST named it: 'the passer term reads the RAW playvol percentile and not recal_96's load-discounted _pv, so a passer under 24 minutes is paid his creation rate twice at full price'. The term now reads minutes through its OWN line, which is STRICTER than recal_96's above 18.4 mpg and LOOSER below it — a 13-minute card keeps 37% of the second payment where the standard path pays him 8%. Composing the two shares was built and measured: it holds all 132 anchors too, at nine more movers and a worst move of -6 instead of -5 (Mark Jackson '03 40 -> 34, T.J. McConnell '16 43 -> 39, John Stockton '85 37 -> 33). The single factor was taken because it is one constant and less collateral; the composed variant is the obvious next step if a ruling ever lands on a sub-20-minute distributor.

THE BAND ANCHORS ARE NOT TOUCHED AND recal_90's WARNING DOES NOT APPLY. Every one of the 224 movers is below the 93 knee, where band() is the identity, so OFF_TOP (102.75) and DEF_TOP (104.25) are byte-identical and not one card above the knee moves. The top 12 by OFF is identical name for name and the top 50 by OVR has no entrant, no leaver and no rank flip.

COLLATERAL IS 224 CARDS ON OFF, EVERY ONE OF THEM DOWN, mean -1.24, max -5, and the shape of it is the doctrine made visible. Only SEVEN cards move by 3 or more and SIX of them are seasons under 24 minutes: Mark Jackson '03 40 -> 36 (17.9 mpg), Ennis Whatley '85 34 -> 31 (19.8), Mark Jackson '91 55 -> 52 (22.2), Muggsy Bogues '89 42 -> 38 (22.2), John Stockton '87 62 -> 57 (22.7), John Stockton '86 54 -> 51 (23.6). The seventh is John Stockton '03 at 27.7. Forty-two cards move by 2 or more. Nobody has ruled on any of them. OVR follows on 153 cards, max -2. DEF moves on ZERO cards and no attribute moves.

EIGHT MORE STOCKTON SEASONS COME DOWN WITH THE SUBJECT and none of them is pinned: '87 62 -> 57, '03 84 -> 81, '00 83 -> 81, '98 81 -> 79, '86 54 -> 51, '02 86 -> 85, '99 74 -> 73, '85 37 -> 35. Every one is a season under 32 minutes; every season of his at 34.7 minutes or more - '88 (34.7), '89, '90, '91, '92, '95, '96, '97 - is byte-identical. That is the ruling's own shape — the seasons he called overrated are the short ones.

WHAT THE ROUND DOES NOT FIX, and a later ruling would have to name it. John Stockton '01 (84) still reads ABOVE his own '90 (82), the 37-minute 17.2-point 14.5-assist season at BPM 8.9. recal_123 decomposed why and it is not this stage's to move: the gap is 10.6 raw points of ZONE ratings (mid 67 / 3pt 66 / rim 49 against 47 / 26 / 56), the pre-1997 seasons are on the INFERRED side of build_ratings.py's FIT_YEARS seam, and data/RATINGS_UPDATE.md ratifies that compression as a known accepted property. Only Tomer can say which end of that seam moves.

notes: THE DEFECT IN ONE SENTENCE: a creation RATE was paid twice — 0.19 x playvol on the standard path and 0.245 x playvol again from recal_109/117's elite-passer term, 34.3 of John Stockton '01's 93-point o_score for one fact — and the second payment carried no reading of the load that produced it at all.

recal_96 IS THE DOCTRINE THIS ROUND APPLIES, NOT A NEW IDEA. It ruled that a per-possession profile must be scaled by the load that produced it and discounts BOTH standard-path load bars by `load_share`. Its full-load line is 24 minutes and it was located by Clint Capela '17 (23.9 mpg) and Ty Jerome '25 — cards on the bench/starter boundary, answering 'did this man play at all'. The second payment of the same rate needs a second line, and it is not the bench boundary: it is the minutes at which a distributor has carried a season's creation.

WHY NOT A SMALLER TERM, settled by arithmetic on two cards rather than by search. John Stockton '90 is pinned 84 +-3 and reads 82: he needs the term to keep g >= 0.916. The subject needs g <= 0.863. The two are playvol 99 apiece, volume 31 against 36, efficiency 97 against 94 and both at gate 1.00 on playvol — NOTHING the term reads separates them. What separates them is 29.2 minutes against 37.4, and that is the only input at this stage that can see it.

WHY NOT THE OTHER HALF OF THE 'READ IT ONCE' FIX, measured and rejected. Fading the standard path's own 0.19 playvol weight as the passer gate opens was built first and it is WORSE, not better: the two Stockton cards have identical playvol (99) and gates within 0.09 of each other, so the fade hits '90 at 86% of the rate it hits '01 — at the largest fade '90's pin permits the subject falls by ONE point, to 85. Against Mark Jackson '98 it is worse still: his gate is 0.966 against the subject's 0.638, so a gate-proportional fade takes 17.3 raw points off him and 12.0 off the subject. The fact IS read twice; what makes the two readings separable is not the fact, it is the load.

MEASURED BEFORE APPLYING, on the whole pool at twelve settings of the line - 33.0, 33.5, 34.0, 34.3, 34.5, 34.7, 35.0, 35.3, 35.6, 36.0, 37.0, 38.0 - the subject reads 85, 85, 84, 84, 84, 84, 84, 84, 84, 84, 83, 83, and the first anchor breaks at 35.3 (Mark Jackson '98), the second at 36.0 (Mark Jackson '99); John Stockton '90 does not move at all until 38.0, and even there he only goes 82 -> 81, still on his floor. 224 of 10,000 cards move on OFF, every one DOWN, max -5, mean -1.24; 153 on OVR, max -2; ZERO on DEF and zero attributes. The top 12 by OFF is identical name for name and the top 50 by OVR has no entrant, no leaver and no rank flip.

THE CLASS IS UNCHANGED — THIS IS A PRICE, NOT A GATE. 834 cards take the term before the round and 834 after it. No card enters the class, none leaves it, and recal_112's efficient interior scorer stays disjoint by construction (its gate is playvol <= 70, this one's foot is 70).
